bullets.title: IREN surges 20% on $2.8B AI cloud contracts; sector read-through to HUT, NBIS
bullets.body: IREN signed $2.8B in new multi-year AI cloud services contracts with Microsoft, Nvidia, Perplexity, and Figure, raising its ARR target to $4B+ and lifting shares ~20%. The company is securing 45% prepayments on new contracts—seen as a bullish neocloud datapoint—and Northland raised NBIS to a $410 price target. HUT gained ~10% following a 15-year $9.8B AI data center lease.

bullets.title: AMD-Microsoft expand AI partnership; Helios GPUs ramping on Azure at scale
bullets.body: AMD and Microsoft announced an expanded strategic partnership deploying AMD Helios Rackscale Solution (MI455X GPUs, EPYC Venice CPUs, Pensando DPUs, ROCm software) on Azure for frontier model inference. The announcement is characterized as AMD's 2H26 inflection point, with OpenAI's first 1GW of MI450 deployment beginning this half.

bullets.title: Google's 'Frozen V2' custom AI chip targets 6-10x token-per-watt efficiency; 2028 deployment
bullets.body: Google is developing Frozen V2 chips with Gemini architecture baked directly into silicon, projected to deliver 6-10x more tokens per unit of power than competitors, with deployment targeted as early as 2028. The company is also reportedly working on Taalas-like chips that embed model weights into silicon, signaling deepening vertical integration in AI compute.

bullets.title: Meta monetizes surplus GPU capacity via Anthropic compute lease
bullets.body: Meta is converting excess AI infrastructure into a cloud business by leasing compute capacity to Anthropic. Multiple sources note this as a new revenue stream leveraging Meta's massive capex investment, alongside Qwen3.8 and DeepSeek V4 extending China's open-weight pricing competition.

bullets.title: Semiconductor sector now 14% of market cap—nearly double dot-com peak
bullets.body: Fintwit commentary flagging that semiconductors represent 14% of total market capitalization, approximately double the ~8% peak during the dot-com bubble. Semis ($SOX) are down 17% month-to-date while the broader market held up, and hedge funds have been net sellers of tech for 6 of the past 8 weeks, cutting exposure ~10% in the largest sector outflow on record.

bullets.title: NVDA showcases agentic/physical AI at SIGGRAPH; NemoClaw and Synthetic Video Detector launched
bullets.body: NVIDIA is using SIGGRAPH 2026 to push agentic and physical AI into creative workflows via NemoClaw (combining Nemotron 3 Ultra, Omniverse, and OpenShell on DGX Station) and a Synthetic Video Detector achieving 92% accuracy on 1080p in 22ms. Samsung's Lee Jae-yong is reportedly visiting Silicon Valley for a potential second meeting with Jensen Huang.

bullets.title: MU crosses $1T market cap; bull case built on FCF vs. TSLA and multi-year DRAM shortage
bullets.body: Micron's market cap crossed $1 trillion, with fintwit bulls arguing MU generated nearly as much FCF last quarter as Tesla has cumulatively. ADATA's chairman warns the DRAM shortage will last another 10 years, with electricity and memory cited as the world's scarcest resources this decade. One analyst projects MU reporting over $70B in revenue in the next two quarters.

bullets.title: TSLA underperforms market pre-earnings; critics flag target misses, valuation, and Musk credibility
bullets.body: Tesla traded lower while the S&P and Nasdaq edged up, with commentary focusing on persistent target misses, an implied EBITDA multiple in Musk's comp package criticized as a 'disgrace,' and a leaked Q2 shareholder deck hinting at hybrid-platform affordable models. One long-term Tesla investor compared MU favorably to TSLA on FCF, risk, and contract visibility.

bullets.title: Paramount-Warner Bros. deal hit with TRO; judge gives 14-day pause, ruling expected July 22
bullets.body: A federal judge issued a temporary restraining order on Paramount's ($PSKY) acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery ($WBD), framed as a judicial freeze ahead of a preliminary injunction battle. Commentary notes Paramount faces a contradiction between leverage claims pitched to Wall Street and what it denies in court, with a ruling expected by July 22.

bullets.title: COHR flagged as strong buy: 29-36% revenue growth, 40%+ adjusted gross margins guided
bullets.body: One fintwit account highlights Coherent as a 'favorite company' with next-quarter guidance of ~$1.98B (+9.6% QoQ, +29.5% YoY), next-four-quarter revenue of $8.5-9.0B (29-36% growth), and exit adjusted gross margins of 40.5-42%.

bullets.title: GOOGL 100-year Sterling debt down 7% since Feb; investment-grade tech debt broadly losing value
bullets.body: Alphabet's century bond has lost more than 7% since its February issuance, driven by duration risk, UK political uncertainty, and a glut of Alphabet debt supply. Commentary notes that investment-grade tech debt issued this year has 'almost universally lost value' amid rising longer-term yields.

bullets.title: Barclays upgrades LITE to Overweight ahead of chip earnings on AI networking demand
bullets.body: Barclays upgraded Lumentum to Overweight citing greater confidence in AI networking and optical components demand ahead of chip earnings, while cutting Allegro and Penguin.

bullets.title: AI pricing fork: US closed-source at $26-56/M tokens vs. Chinese open-weight at $0.50-1/M
bullets.body: Chamath and others highlight the AI market has bifurcated into closed-source US models ($26-56 per 1MM tokens) and Chinese open-weight alternatives ($0.50-1 per 1MM tokens)—a 50-100x cost gap. Chamath also called tokenmaxxing on frontier models 'a bridge to nowhere and money-burning furnace,' while Ramp reports average token spend surged 21x over 12 months.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler FCF 'collapse' narrative pushed back; OCF at records despite high capex
bullets.body: One fintwit account characterizes posts framing hyperscaler free cash flow as 'collapsing' as 'pure fear porn,' arguing OCF remains at record levels and that high capex is being mischaracterized. Goldman Sachs separately flagged that $5.3T in AI spending by Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet through 2030 could exert pressure on bond markets.

bullets.title: AAPL hits record 11x price-to-sales, highest valuation in company history
bullets.body: Apple is now trading at nearly 11x sales, the highest price-to-sales ratio in the company's history, with one fintwit account flagging the metric as notable versus its historical range.

bullets.title: SPY gamma negative; $2.3B put wall at 740; $10M+ SOXX call LEAPS detected
bullets.body: Options flow commentary shows SPY gamma remains negative with a $2.3B put wall at the 740 strike, while separately $10M+ in call LEAPS were detected on the semiconductor ETF $SOXX, suggesting bifurcated positioning heading into hyperscaler earnings week.

bullets.title: Leading Economic Index misses at -0.2%; US large-company bankruptcies at 16-year high
bullets.body: The Conference Board Leading Economic Index fell 0.2% MoM in June, missing the -0.1% estimate and reversing the prior month's +0.1% gain. Separately, U.S. large-company bankruptcies hit 372 in H1 2026—a 16-year high and the fourth consecutive YoY increase.

bullets.title: 10-year Treasury yield at 4.60%; UK 30-year gilt hits highest since May at 5.749%
bullets.body: The 10-year US Treasury yield is back at 4.60%, while UK 30-year gilt yields spiked 8bps to 5.749%—the highest since May 20—following new PM Burnham's comments on fiscal flexibility. Former NY Fed president Dudley expects pressure on the Fed to tighten by fall.

bullets.title: Bernstein raises HOOD price target to $160 on $70B+ prediction market fee opportunity
bullets.body: Bernstein raised its Robinhood price target from $130 to $160, citing a $70B+ trading fee pool across prediction markets, perpetual futures, tokenized equities, and onchain assets. The firm highlights Robinhood's 27M-user distribution advantage as a key competitive edge.

bullets.title: 92% S&P 500 earnings beat rate; Goldman says market bottom 'still a couple of weeks away'
bullets.body: 92% of S&P 500 companies have beaten earnings estimates so far this season. However, Goldman's One-Delta Desk raised concerns about AI capex cycle sustainability and suggested the market bottom is 'still a couple of weeks away,' while commentary on price-driven (rather than narrative-driven) dynamics and retail influence flags tactical trading dominance.
